comparator.name: Econometrics and Operations Research
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted TiSEM 2026–2027 EER v4, pp.75–77, gives the full September-2026 entrant curriculum through 2028–2029. It controls the public overview where they differ. The non-exchange Cluster A pathway is first in the adopted table; optional study abroad follows and is constrained by equivalent EOR/philosophy study. This example selects four Autumn Cluster A courses, Combinatorial Optimization, Computational Aspects in Econometrics, Data Analytics for Non-Life Insurance and Games and Economic Behavior, plus Spring Auctions, Bargaining and Networks. All three required fields are represented. The sixth course, Spring Econometrics for Policy Analysis, fills the six-credit elective under the permitted additional-Cluster-A option. With Autumn Philosophy of Science and Statistics, and Spring Philosophy and History of Economic Thought and thesis, each final-year semester totals thirty credits. The current 30L310-B-6 catalogue agrees with the adopted philosophy title rather than the public Economic Ethics wording. There is no thirty-credit unrestricted mobility block in this selected route. First-year Probability and Statistics spans two blocks but counts six credits only once. Improving Society Lab activities in the first year are non-credit; its six credits count once in year two. Grow and software workshops are extracurricular/zero-credit. EER 4.5.7(iii) and the thesis entry both require 144 EC including Improving Society Lab; the example has 150 EC before starting the Spring thesis. No additional insurance, finance or OR electives are added.
components: Macroeconomics for Econometrics and Operational Research
Microeconomics for Econometrics and Operational Research
This applied quantitative-modelling course runs across the first two years. Its six credits are counted once in year two; the first-year activities do not add separate credits.
A selected Business Analytics and Operations Research Cluster A course. Linear Optimization and Advanced Linear Algebra provide its entry preparation.
A selected Econometrics and Mathematical Economics Cluster A course, covering SQL databases, Python data processing and scientific computation.
A selected Quantitative Finance and Actuarial Science Cluster A course, studying insurance and credit risk, credibility and claims reserving.
A fourth selected Cluster A course, studying strategic and cooperative economic interaction.
A fifth selected Cluster A course, studying bargaining, networks and auctions. Together the five selected courses provide thirty credits and include all three required fields.
Philosophy and History of Economic Thought
The additional six-credit elective is filled by a different Cluster A course, Econometrics for Policy Analysis. It is not counted among the five courses making up the thirty-credit cluster.

The twelve-credit thesis is independent research in econometrics or operations research, written and presented in English. Entry requires at least 144 completed credits including the Improving Society Lab. The example completes 150 credits before the Spring thesis starts.

Microeconomics, macroeconomics, public economics and financial appraisal supply substantive applications; data analysis, statistical methods and ethical reflection support responsible quantitative decisions.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no formal route. The adopted cohort table first presents the five-course Cluster A pathway and then optional study abroad. The first valid non-exchange pathway is selected independently of UCR fit. Four first-listed Autumn subjects and the first Spring subject satisfy the three-field minimum while keeping thirty EC per semester. The six-credit elective selects the first remaining Spring Cluster A subject under the explicit permitted option.

selection.assessment: The closest quantitative economics/econometrics/optimisation response is complemented sequentially by a computational-business-analytics direction and an economic/financial-decision direction. Their actual priorities and feasible selections differ materially and meet the four-course distinctness floor. Quantitative methods for societal challenges are substantively owned by the closest public-economics and empirical-modelling core, rather than hidden in a residual data-science candidate. Actuarial science is a separately evidenced candidate, stopped at the three-programme maximum; no unconstructed fourth programme or absence-based academic no-match is claimed.

blocks: Both develop reflective competence assessment, learning goals and academic/professional choices. UCR also includes civic engagement, academic writing and collaborative inquiry.

Both evaluate financial investments using discounting and quantitative appraisal. UCR adds accounting and corporate budgeting; Tilburg also develops insurance, pension and stochastic financial models.

Both examine pricing and risk of financial contracts. Tilburg adds CAPM/factor models and econometric asset-return analysis; UCR combines market pricing with banks, monetary policy and balance-sheet risk decisions.

Both use formal models of consumers, production, market structure and allocation. UCR also introduces macroeconomics; Tilburg emphasises explicit solutions and additional uncertainty/information problems.
Both use economic models to study output, inflation, employment, growth and policy, including international relationships. The mathematical treatment and applications differ.

Both analyse strategic market behaviour, competition and economic choice through formal models. Tilburg concentrates on normal/extensive-form games, spatial/dynamic competition and entry; UCR spans wider microeconomic topics.

Both evaluate economic policy with models and empirical evidence. UCR centres efficiency, equity, tax and public-expenditure questions; Tilburg develops dedicated micro-causal identification and dynamic macroeconometric methods.

Both develop regression estimation and instrumental-variable methods with empirical economic applications in Stata. Tilburg derives more finite-sample and asymptotic properties; UCR additionally emphasises GLS, tests and Monte Carlo illustration.

Both examine reasoning biases and departures from rational economic choice. UCR develops behavioural economic models and experiments; Tilburg additionally investigates scientific method, probability interpretations and the evidence supplied by statistical models.

Both use probabilistic and Markov-style models for uncertainty. UCR concentrates on beliefs and sequential decisions; Tilburg develops Markov and branching processes, queues, inventory and service-operation models.
Both develop elementary mathematical proof, including induction and contradiction. UCR centres logic and discrete structures; Tilburg also reviews algebra, differentiation and integration.

Both formulate and solve constrained linear/discrete optimisation problems. Tilburg develops simplex, duality, shadow prices, branch-and-bound and cuts; UCR places linear/discrete optimisation in a broader search and AI toolkit.

Both study relational data models and SQL. Tilburg combines that module with Python data processing and scientific computing for econometrics; UCR develops relational database management more specifically.

Both study greedy and dynamic programming, network-flow/optimisation algorithms and their performance. Tilburg additionally centres routing, scheduling, integer formulations and approximation quality.
Both introduce Python, data collections, recursion, object-oriented programming and computational problem solving.

Both study single-variable limits, differentiation, integration and series. Tilburg emphasises mathematical theorems and proofs; UCR develops analytical/computational techniques and dynamic-model applications.
Both study linear systems, vectors, matrices, spaces and transformations. Their mix of proof, computational methods and applications differs.

Both solve differential-equation and integration problems. UCR centres numerical approximation, algorithms, stability and error; Tilburg centres analytical linear systems, convergence, measures and Riemann/Stieltjes/Lebesgue integration.

Both extend calculus to functions of several variables for quantitative modelling. Tilburg develops the mathematical theory and proofs; UCR includes differential equations and computer-algebra applications.

Both develop multivariate probability, estimation, confidence intervals and simulation. Tilburg emphasises limit theorems and estimator properties; UCR additionally includes Bayesian reasoning and sampling algorithms.

Both select, apply and interpret statistical procedures and uncertainty. Tilburg develops estimator, confidence-interval, testing and nonparametric theory; UCR uses behavioural data, experimental design and multivariable models.
Mathematical probability is developed in the course aligned to the separate Probability and Statistics unit; it is not counted twice.
The selected linear algebra course is placed with the first dedicated unit; no second selected course reproduces the additional proof-based advanced linear-algebra sequence.
Academic writing and presentation support the selected courses, but none is counted again as this separate EOR communication-skills unit.

The selected econometrics course is placed with the stronger introductory OLS/IV/Stata relationship. No additional course supplies this separate nonlinear, GMM, maximum-likelihood and asymptotic-theory sequence.
Selected courses include empirical and computational projects, but none is counted again as the separate integrated EOR society-lab requirement.
Probability, learning and financial evidence provide relevant foundations, but no selected course centres insurance-portfolio pricing, credibility and claims reserving.
Strategic choices and discrete reasoning appear in selected courses, but none is counted again as the dedicated non-cooperative/cooperative economic-game theory unit.
No selected course centres axiomatic bargaining, auction equilibria, Shapley values and network power.
General ethical reasoning complements normative reflection, but no selected course centres the historical development and ethical assumptions of economic thought.
The independent econometric or operations-research thesis remains compulsory. Optional UCR independent research is additional to the scheduled 180 credits.

notes.text: UCR combines economic and financial study with mathematical, statistical and computational methods. Tilburg provides a more prescribed mathematical-econometric sequence, specialist Cluster A courses spanning three fields, an integrated society lab and an independent thesis. The relationships shown are partial.

audience.programmeDescription: Econometrics and Operations Research at Tilburg uses mathematics, statistics and computational models to investigate economic and organisational problems. This non-exchange example selects Combinatorial Optimization, Computational Aspects in Econometrics, Data Analytics for Non-Life Insurance, Games and Economic Behavior, Auctions, Bargaining and Networks, and Econometrics for Policy Analysis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR can emphasise quantitative economics and optimisation, computational data science, or economic and financial decisions with quantitative methods. Tilburg has a more prescribed proof-based mathematics and econometrics sequence, specialist courses across operations research, economics and insurance, a society lab and a required independent thesis. The relationships shown are partial.
